page: Microsoft Azure HB368-48rs_v5 is a high-performance computing instance within the HBv5 series, tailored for memory-intensive simulations, large-scale data analytics, and I/O-heavy enterprise workloads. It operates on Microsoft Hyper-V virtualization with 48 dedicated x86_64 vCPUs powered by Intel processor architecture, offering 448 GB of system memory that yields an allocation of 9.33 GB per core.

For storage-bound and parallel execution environments, the instance provides 15,874 GB of integrated local NVMe SSD storage alongside support for Premium Storage tiers. It features native RDMA networking support to enable low-latency node-to-node communication across clustered environments. No discrete graphics processors are included.

Cost efficiency reflects its specialized resource provisioning, prioritizing a substantial 9.33:1 memory-to-core ratio and massive local scratch disk space over raw core density. The trade-off is a constrained core count relative to other nodes in the family, making it optimal for licenses bound to core counts or memory-bound computational fluid dynamics, large in-memory databases, and high-throughput data pipelines.
description: Microsoft Azure HB368-48rs_v5 is a specialized high-performance computing instance built for memory-heavy and I/O-intensive workloads. Powered by an x86_64 Intel processor architecture and managed by Microsoft Hyper-V, the system provides 48 dedicated vCPUs coupled with 448 GB of RAM, translating to an expansive 9.33 GB of memory per core. The instance integrates 15,874 GB of high-speed local NVMe SSD storage and includes support for both Premium Storage and RDMA networking, allowing efficient node interconnectivity without discrete GPU hardware. With zero bundled public IPv4 addresses, access is structured for private cloud infrastructure. This configuration offers high qualitative value for computational tasks constrained by memory footprints, high-throughput local caching, or core-based software licensing costs rather than absolute CPU core parallelization. It serves demanding enterprise databases, memory-bound simulations, ETL pipelines, and high-performance computing clusters requiring low-latency network interconnects.
